children: Ohio reported its first flu-associated pediatric death of the 2026-27 season, a teenager under 18 from Ross County, the state health department said on Friday.
Ohio generally records between one and seven pediatric flu deaths each season, according to the department.

The Ohio health department urged everyone six months or older to receive an updated flu vaccine, saying vaccination can reduce severe illness and hospitalization even when it does not prevent infection.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention rates flu activity in Ohio as low, but state officials said hospitalizations typically rise toward year-end. They said hospitalizations last season climbed sharply beginning in December before peaking in January and again in mid-February.
The death comes during an unusually early US flu season dominated by H1N1, a strain with a new mutation that scientists say may leave younger people with less previous immunity.
Seasonal flu activity continues to increase nationally, with two pediatric deaths reported in the week ending November 14, bringing the season's total to seven, according to the CDC.
The US Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
